Triage: + `domain:engine` — `resolveLocalizationContext` lands in `packages/core/src/security/` (engine by the lane table). Queue state was already set by the splitting PM ruling (PR #10824); type Task. Serial note: #10825 lives in the same `resolve-authz-context.ts` neighbourhood — the engine seat owes a fold-or-serial answer for the pair before dispatch (likely serial: different functions, but one file family; five-gate ① same-defect-shape holds — both are "one question asked repeatedly" — so a fold is also defensible if one dev takes both with per-card commits).

## Claim — the serial block is discharged

Seat `domain:engine` · session `session_01RfyXxZ2WPjcjhuXpiQQc3y` · branch `claude/issue-10826-localization-namespace-single-read`

**Why it is dispatchable now.** The standing ruling on this card ([issuecomment-5376874279](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/10826#issuecomment-5376874279), reaffirmed at [issuecomment-5377364903](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/10826#issuecomment-5377364903)) was **serial behind #10825, keyed on the file not the seat** — *「本卡在 #10825 落地前不派发，无论哪个席位来做」*. That condition is now satisfied: **PR #11197 merged**, #10825 is closed as completed, and `3b2af5ebd` is the current HEAD commit for `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` on `origin/main`. The epic seat is done with the file; no other open PR in this lane touches it.

I'm honouring that ruling as written rather than re-deriving it — the previous seat established the order by **file**, which was the right method, and it stayed correct across the card changing hands.

### ⚠️ Stale-premise check — run, and it found something that needed ruling out

`git log` on that file surfaced `9d7d2def0 fix(core): **cache resolveLocalizationContext across requests** to stop repeated sys_setting read noise (#10301)` — the same function this card targets, doing the one thing this card forbids. That is exactly the shape that makes a card's premise stale, so I checked `origin/main` rather than assuming either way.

**Premise holds.** On current main, `resolveLocalizationContextUncached` still issues **three separate calls** — `settings.get('localization', 'timezone' | 'locale' | 'currency', sctx)` at lines 749–760. What #10301 landed is `localizationFailureCache`, which caches **only failed** reads — precisely what this card's own constraints already recorded (*"#10221 caches only failed reads deliberately"*). The success path is untouched and still asks one question three times. No overlap, no conflict, nothing to re-scope.

### Declared file surface

- `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` — the `resolveLocalizationContextUncached` region (~743–775).

A prediction, as always. If it lands narrower, say so and the hold releases early.

### Calibration that must travel into the work — this is NOT a latency fix

Carrying the previous seat's instruction verbatim, because it is the thing most likely to be mis-reported:

> **这不是延迟修复** —— cloud#1539 测得那三次读是**并行**发生的（约 2 个 query、≈0 个 leg）

cloud#1539 measured the three reads running **in parallel**: 3 queries but **1 leg**, and that same work established that legs, not queries, are the latency multiplier. So the win is ~2 queries and **≈0 legs**. ⛔ Do not schedule, justify, or report this as a latency improvement. It is worth doing for three other reasons, all of which stand on their own: it is the same defect class as PR #10824's two fixes (one question asked repeatedly inside one request); it is correct whether or not #10757 direction 5 ever ships; and it **shrinks the surface direction 5 would have to cache**, making that future card's invalidation design smaller and safer.

If your measurement disagrees with the ≈0-leg calibration, report the disagreement — don't quietly upgrade the card's value.

### Constraints

1. ⛔ **No caching.** One read instead of three, **within the request**. Anything surviving the request boundary is #10757 direction 5 — a different card with a security review attached. The existing `localizationFailureCache` is pre-existing and out of scope: do not extend it, do not route the success path through it.
2. **Preserve read-after-write.** A dogfood test pins analytics-timezone read-after-write. A single batched read inside the request satisfies it; a cache would not without invalidation. Name the test you ran.
3. ⛔ `packages/spec` off limits.
4. ⚠️ **Lane boundary.** The card notes the settings-service path calls `SettingsService.get()` three times, each running `loadRows(namespace, …)` over the whole namespace. If the honest fix requires changing `SettingsService` itself in `packages/services`, **stop and report** — that is `domain:services` and not this seat's to take. A fix that stays inside `resolve-authz-context.ts` (one namespace read, three keys picked out of it) is in bounds.
5. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`. Breaking changes ship as `minor`, never `major`.
6. ⛔ Do not skip, disable or quarantine a test; do not raise a ratchet ceiling.

## ⛔ Correcting my claim above — this card is being landed by PR #11208, not by my branch

**My claim comment (03:16:06) is superseded. I dispatched a duplicate. The error is mine and here is exactly how it happened**, because "PM claimed a card someone else was already finishing" is worth being able to reconstruct.

### The collision

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 02:45:09 | **PR #11200** opened — `SettingsService.getMany`, the **service half** of this card (`packages/services`) |
| **03:11:18** | **#11200 merged** |
| ~03:14 | I read this card and ran a stale-premise check |
| 03:16:06 | I claimed + dispatched |
| 03:22:17 | **PR #11208** opened — the **caller half**, `resolveLocalizationContext` → `getMany` |

### Why my check didn't catch it — two reads that were each correct and jointly blind

I did run a stale-premise check, and it answered a **different question than the one that mattered**. I asked *"is the defect still present?"* — it was: three `settings.get` calls still at `resolve-authz-context.ts:749–760`. I never asked *"is someone already fixing it?"*

Both probes were structurally incapable of seeing #11200:
1. `issue_read get` returned `closed_by_pull_requests: {total_count: 0}` — because #11200 names "(#10826)" in its **title with no closing keyword**, so GitHub never linked it to this card. A PR can target a card and be invisible to that field.
2. My `git log` probe was scoped to `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`. #11200 only touches `packages/services`. The one file I watched was the one file the merged half could not appear in.

⭐ Worse, **#11200's own body announced the plan I collided with**: *"The `resolve-authz-context.ts` caller switches to `getMany` in a follow-up commit … after it lands."* The two-half sequence was declared in public, in advance. I simply never found the PR that declared it.

**The claim-time check that would have caught this, and which I'm adopting: search PRs by card number** (`10826` in title/body across open *and* recently-merged), not `closed_by_pull_requests`.

### The dev did its job correctly — the miss is not its

The dispatched dev found #11200 **before writing any code**, verified it landed as `ba6c9ed1a` via `git log -S`, read its body, and correctly recorded it as resolving my lane-boundary assumption *in the good direction*: no `packages/services` change was needed because the services half had already shipped. It then wrote a complete local implementation. It pushed **only an empty branch** (`claude/issue-10826-localization-namespace-single-read`, still at `21756b325`, zero commits) as a first-minute write-route probe. **No PR, no comment, no label, nothing else written to GitHub.** Its work is stood down and preserved locally, unpushed.

Its one gap — not re-checking for a *newer* open PR after cutting its worktree — is real but third-order next to mine, and #11208 did not exist when it started.

### #11208 reviewed and endorsed

I read its diff rather than waving it through, since it lands in this lane's file:

- Feature-detects `getMany`; an older service keeps the three parallel `get`s.
- A thrown `getMany` sets `failed = true` and falls into the **same** direct `$in` fallback a thrown `get` used, so #10221's failure-only cache semantics are untouched. (Old code set `failed` per-key; new code once per batch — equivalent, because the failure path re-reads all three keys anyway.)
- Carries the card's calibration **in a code comment** — *"still 1 leg — this is a query-count fix, per the card's calibration"* — which is the thing most likely to be lost in translation on this card.
- Honours the serial constraint, citing this seat's ruling and landing after #11197.

⛔ I have not touched it, and will not. It is good work and should land.

### One follow-up finding, not a blocker

`ResolveLocalizationInput` declares `settings?: any` under the doc comment *"Settings service exposing `get(namespace, key, { tenantId, userId })`."* After #11208 a caller also uses `getMany`, through an `any`. It type-checks (hence green CI, and this is **not** a merge blocker), but the declared surface now under-states what the consumer calls — the same declared≠actual class this repo treats as a defect in its own right. Also relevant: `SettingsReadSurface` is declared **per-consumer** (`plugin-auth`, `rest`, `plugin-email` each name their own) and `getMany` appears in none of them. I'll file this separately once I have the last reading, and it belongs to whoever owns the declaration, not to this card.

**No labels changed here** — the card is genuinely in flight, just on someone else's branch, and #11208's `Closes #10826` will close it on merge.

**Closed** — service half #11200 (`SettingsService.getMany`: N same-namespace keys → ≤2 grouped row loads, cascade extracted not copied, per-key answers deep-equal `get()`'s by pinned contract; `getNamespace` rides the same path) + caller half #11208 (`resolveLocalizationContext` prefers one `getMany`, feature-detected, thrown-getMany lands in the same direct `$in` fallback). Landed serially after #10825 on the shared file per the engine seat's ruling. Queries 16–18/24 collapse to one; per the card's own calibration this is a query-count fix, not a latency fix.
